guide.title: Academic Interpretation Guide (Hair et al., 2021)
guide.ci_desc: The optimal non-parametric method in PLS-SEM to evaluate parameter stability without relying on distributional assumptions.
guide.sig_desc: A parameter is statistically significant at α = 0.05 if its 95% CI does not contain zero. This is the gold standard used alongside p-values.
guide.power_desc: With {{iterations}} iterations, the algorithm ensures highly precise standard error estimation, limiting Type I errors.

recommendation.title: Reporting Recommendations (APA 7)
recommendation.report_desc: Report the original sample estimate along with the 95% CI (e.g., β = 0.35, 95% CI [0.12, 0.51]) in hypothesis testing tables.
recommendation.width_desc: The CI width (Upper - Lower) reflects estimation precision. A very wide CI indicates low precision (due to small sample size or high data variance) and should be noted as a limitation.
recommendation.hypothesis_desc: For path coefficients where the CI contains zero, the corresponding hypothesis must be rejected (not supported).

mga.title: MGA Results
mga.subtitle: Multi-Group Analysis - Comparing between groups
mga.sig_desc_yes: ✅ Groups have a significant difference in mean values
mga.sig_desc_no: ⚠️ Groups do not have a significant difference in mean values

guide.title: Academic Interpretation Guide (MGA)
guide.mga_desc: Tests whether parameter estimates (e.g., means, path coefficients) differ significantly between two or more groups, thereby uncovering unobserved heterogeneity.
guide.sig_desc: Rejects the null hypothesis (H0) of homogeneity. A statistically significant difference exists between the groups.
guide.nonsig_desc: Fails to reject H0. The assumption that the data stems from the same population remains plausible.

recommendation.title: Reporting Recommendations (APA 7)
recommendation.implications_desc: Given the significant difference, pooled analysis is inappropriate. Strategies or conclusions should be tailored to each specific group.
recommendation.advantage_desc: Group {{group}} exhibits the highest levels. Underlying factors for this advantage should be explored in the discussion.
recommendation.limitation_desc: Group {{group}} has the lowest levels. Consider proposing targeted policy interventions for this cohort.
recommendation.pooled_desc: Since no systematic difference was found, data can be pooled to increase sample size (N) and statistical power for the overall structural model.

guide.title: Academic Interpretation Guide (IPMA)
guide.q1_desc: Constructs with above-average importance but below-average performance. These represent major bottlenecks requiring immediate strategic intervention.
guide.q2_desc: High importance and high performance. The organization should maintain current resources allocated to these constructs.
guide.q3_desc: High performance but low overall contribution to the target construct. Consider reallocating resources away from these areas.
guide.q4_desc: Low importance and low performance. Do not prioritize additional investment here.

recommendation.title: Managerial Implications (APA 7)
recommendation.urgent_desc1: Managerial action should focus strictly on
recommendation.urgent_desc2: to achieve the most effective improvement of the target construct at the lowest opportunity cost.
recommendation.defensive_desc2: as these represent core competitive advantages.
recommendation.report: Report the IPMA scatter plot alongside this index table to enrich the Discussion section.

procedure.title: Procedure Details
procedure.omitted_points_desc: Total data points masked for predictive validation.

guide.title: Q² Interpretation Guide (Predictive Relevance)
guide.q2_positive_desc: The model has out-of-sample predictive relevance. Model predictions outperform the naive mean.
guide.q2_zero_desc: Negligible predictive power, roughly equivalent to predicting the mean.
guide.q2_negative_desc: The model lacks predictive relevance entirely. Structural predictions are worse than the naive mean.

methodology.title: Blindfolding Methodology
methodology.intro: Blindfolding is a resampling technique based on Cross-Validation:
methodology.algorithm_desc: Systematically deletes data points at distance D = {{distance}}.
methodology.estimation_desc: The PLS model is re-estimated using the remaining data.
methodology.prediction_desc: The estimated parameters are used to predict the masked data points.
methodology.evaluation_desc: The Q² (Stone-Geisser) metric is calculated based on prediction errors.

recommendation.title: Reporting Recommendations (APA 7)
recommendation.report_q2_desc: The Q² value must be reported for each reflective endogenous latent construct.
recommendation.effect_size_desc: High-impact journals often require the q² effect size to evaluate the relative predictive contribution of individual exogenous constructs.
recommendation.applicability_desc: Do NOT apply or interpret Q² for exogenous constructs or formative endogenous constructs.

guide.title: Interpretation Guide
guide.red_cells_desc: indicate potential discriminant validity issues. Consider revising your measurement model.

actions.title: Recommended Actions
actions.review_desc: Check if items are loading on the correct factors
actions.remove_desc: Consider removing items that cause high HTMT values
actions.alternative_desc: Consider using Fornell-Larcker criterion as additional evidence

methodology.title: Methodology: HTMT Criterion
methodology.method_desc: HTMT (Heterotrait-Monotrait Ratio) assesses discriminant validity by comparing the average correlations between items measuring different constructs to the average correlations between items measuring the same construct.
methodology.strict_desc: Strict criterion (0.85) recommended for conceptually similar constructs
methodology.lenient_desc: Lenient criterion (0.90) acceptable for conceptually distinct constructs

ttest_ui.levene_test: Levene's Test for Equality of Variances
